definitions.explanation: Not carrying or bringing anything, especially when visiting someone or attending an event where bringing something (a gift, supplies, etc.) would be expected.

examples.japanese: {手|て}ぶらで⟦{来|き}て→来る：00254_kuru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.notes: A common polite phrase telling guests not to bring gifts.

examples.japanese: {手|て}ぶらで⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{失礼|しつれい}→失礼：01247_shitsurei⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}った→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: I thought it would be rude to go empty-handed.

examples.japanese: ⟦キャンプ→キャンプ：03837_kyanpu⟧{場|じょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{手|て}ぶらで⟦バーベキュー→バーベキュー：27519_baabekyuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{楽|たの}しめる→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧⟦プラン→プラン：00345_puran⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: The campground has a plan where you can enjoy barbecue without bringing anything.
examples.notes: {手|て}ぶらで is commonly used in advertising for services that provide everything.

notes:
{手|て}ぶら means being empty-handed — not carrying anything or not bringing anything along. It often carries cultural significance in Japanese social contexts, where bringing a gift (⟦{手|て}{土産|みやげ}→手土産：08353_temiyage⟧) when visiting is expected.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {手|て}ぶら⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧: to come empty-handed
- {手|て}ぶら⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go without bringing anything
- {手|て}ぶらで⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧: to go back empty-handed (without achieving anything)
- {手|て}ぶらでOK: no need to bring anything (casual/advertising)

NOTE: In recent years, {手|て}ぶら is increasingly used in marketing phrases like {手|て}ぶら⟦キャンプ→キャンプ：03837_kyanpu⟧ (camping with all equipment provided) and {手|て}ぶら⟦バーベキュー→バーベキュー：27519_baabekyuu⟧ (BBQ with everything supplied).
